$comment: Context package loaded by the developer agent before it begins work.
Contains file paths and expectations only. No credentials, tokens, secrets,
connection strings or Fabric identifiers. Real environment values live in

ticketSource.$comment: The active ticket is the GitHub Issue named in the execution manifest written into the worktree. Its body is supplied by the dispatcher, never hardcoded here.

expectations.useDeterministicScriptsNote: Any Fabric operation performed more than once belongs in scripts/ as a parameterised, re-runnable script. Do not re-improvise an API sequence per session.
expectations.verifyRuntimeStateNote: An HTTP 200, 201 or 202 means a request was accepted, not that it took effect. Every mutation is followed by a read-back of actual state. Evidence from a response body alone is not evidence.
expectations.neverInferIdentifiersNote: Workspace, folder and item identifiers come from the ticket and config/environment.local.json, never deduced from a naming convention, the only plausible candidate, or what was used last time. Ambiguity is a stop condition.
expectations.resolveTargetBeforeWritingNote: The authorised target is per-ticket. Resolve it to its REST folder GUID and verify it exists before any write. A folder name is not an address.
expectations.prefixTicketScopedItemsNote: Item display names are unique per WORKSPACE, not per folder, so the issue-number prefix is the real collision-avoidance control.
expectations.allowlistCoversDataPathsNote: Items live in folders; Lakehouse tables do not. An item-only allowlist lets an inventory come back clean while table contents were overwritten.
expectations.scopeDiscipline: Modify only what the ticket allows. Work discovered outside that scope becomes a new Issue, not an addition to this one.

prohibited: committing or pushing to a protected branch
creating a workspace or service principal
deleting, renaming or overwriting an existing Fabric item
deploying outside the target authorised by the active ticket
inferring a Fabric workspace, folder or item identifier
writing a credential, token, password, key or connection string to any file, argument, log, commit or evidence record
resolving a documentation/ticket conflict by editing the documentation
weakening a safety control in order to complete a ticket

handoff.note: The developer prepares work for review and never merges. Merge is a human decision.
